title: Payroll Software Comparison for Growing Teams
description: A side-by-side comparison of payroll platforms including Gusto, ADP, Rippling, Paychex, and QuickBooks Payroll, covering pricing models, automation, tax compliance, and multi-state payroll support.
body:
Payroll processing is one of the highest-stakes HR functions. Errors in wage calculation, tax withholding, or filing deadlines can result in penalties, employee dissatisfaction, and regulatory exposure. Choosing the right payroll software requires evaluating accuracy, automation, compliance coverage, and total cost across organizational growth stages.

This comparison examines five payroll platforms commonly evaluated by growing organizations. None of the platforms have published pricing verification data at the time of writing, so check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Gusto

Gusto is the leading choice for small businesses with straightforward payroll needs. The platform handles federal, state, and local tax filing automatically across all fifty states, including new hire reporting and W-2 generation.

Gusto's full-service payroll model means that the vendor assumes liability for tax filing accuracy. If Gusto makes a tax filing error, Gusto covers the penalties, providing meaningful risk reduction for small business owners who lack dedicated payroll expertise.

The platform's limitations become apparent for organizations with complex pay structures. Commission-only employees, tipped workers, piece-rate pay, and union deductions may require manual configuration or exceed Gusto's automation capabilities.

Check Gusto's current pricing page for exact rates. Gusto's base plan includes payroll processing for a set number of employees, with additional per-employee charges above the base allowance.

## ADP

ADP's payroll capabilities serve organizations of all sizes, from small businesses through global enterprises. The ADP RUN platform serves small employers, while Workforce Now scales to mid-market and enterprise needs.

ADP's compliance infrastructure is unmatched. The platform supports all fifty states plus territories, handles complex multi-state taxation for remote and mobile workforces, and provides automated garnishment processing. ADP also offers workers compensation administration and retirement plan integration.

The trade-off is interface complexity and minimum commitment requirements. ADP's small business plans may require annual commitments, and the platform's configuration options can feel overwhelming for organizations with simple payroll needs.

Check ADP's current pricing page for exact rates. ADP's pricing varies significantly based on headcount, service level, and geographic coverage.

## Rippling

Rippling's payroll module integrates with its broader HR, IT, and finance platform, creating automated workflows that connect payroll to employee lifecycle events. When a new hire is onboarded in Rippling, payroll setup, benefits enrollment, and tax withholding configuration happen automatically.

Rippling's payroll strengths include global contractor payment support, automatic tax filing in all fifty states, and tight integration with the platform's time tracking, expense management, and benefits administration modules.

Organizations that only need standalone payroll processing may find Rippling's platform approach excessive. The payroll module is most valuable when used alongside Rippling's HRIS and IT management capabilities.

Check Rippling's current pricing page for exact rates. Rippling pricing is typically bundled across selected product lines.

## Paychex

Paychex serves small to mid-market organizations with a focus on local service delivery. The platform provides payroll processing, tax compliance, and HR administration through a combination of software and dedicated service representatives.

Paychex's differentiation is its local market expertise. The company maintains compliance infrastructure for all fifty states with locally staffed service teams that understand regional employment regulations. This local service model appeals to organizations that value in-person or regional phone support over self-service portals.

The platform's technology interface lags behind Gusto and Rippling in modern design and mobile capabilities. Paychex's value proposition is service quality rather than technological innovation.

Check Paychex's current pricing page for exact rates. Paychex pricing typically includes a base processing fee plus per-employee charges.

## QuickBooks Payroll

QuickBooks Payroll integrates directly with QuickBooks accounting software, making it the natural choice for organizations that use QuickBooks for financial management. Payroll data flows directly to the general ledger, eliminating manual reconciliation.

The platform offers three tiers: basic payroll calculation, full-service tax filing, and premium service with HR support. Tax penalty protection is included on full-service plans, similar to Gusto's liability model.

QuickBooks Payroll's limitation is its dependency on the QuickBooks ecosystem. Organizations using other accounting software face integration challenges and may be better served by standalone payroll platforms.

Check QuickBooks Payroll's current pricing page for exact rates. Pricing varies by plan tier and headcount.

## Selection Guidance

The right payroll platform balances automation, compliance coverage, and cost against organizational complexity. Small businesses benefit from Gusto's full-service model and penalty protection. Growing companies with expanding headcount should evaluate Rippling's automated workflows. Enterprises with multi-state and multi-country requirements need ADP's compliance infrastructure.
